# #1574: Patch: the fuzz's forged probes cover malformed prompt answers and unlisted activations
Opened by @jgoetzmann-bot.

## What it actually means
The fuzz already proves the engine refuses a replayed nonce, a wrong-seat action, and an attack or position switch the client was never offered. Two other forged-input classes go unchecked: a malformed prompt answer — a missing pick, a doubled pick, an option the prompt never offered, a choice that belongs to the other seat — and an Activate the legal list never listed. Since the server reduces whatever a client sends without consulting the legal list, these refusals are what stand between a forged packet and a moved game. After this, both are forged and verified refused under the same probe machinery.

## Why
`unlisted_accepted` forges only `SwitchPosition` and `Attack` (`crates/engine/src/testkit/invariants.rs` I8 region ~955-1003), while `activation_actions` enumerates `Activate`/`ActivatePower` for every own and either-player field card (`crates/engine/src/reduce.rs:958-988`) — an accepted-but-unlisted activation is the same exploit class I8 exists to catch (a reused once-per-turn ability, an activation under a restriction, a wrong-seat either-player ability). And `prompts.rs` validates answers on identity, seat, pick cardinality, option membership, duplicates and budget — every one of those branches is only unit-tested, never probed for soundness in situ.

## Proposal
Extend `unlisted_accepted` to forge activations (enumerate candidate instances/abilities on the state), and add a malformed-answer probe that mutates a live prompt's answer — dropped pick, duplicated pick, out-of-set option, other seat's `choice_id` — through the same clone-and-reduce harness, on the existing probe stride.

## Where it lands
`crates/engine/src/testkit/invariants.rs` and its fuzz wiring in `crates/tools/src/fuzz.rs`; spec §10.6 (prompts), §10.2 (actions).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] On a seed holding an activate-able board, unlisted activations are forged and any acceptance fails the run
- [ ] On a seed with an open prompt, each malformed-answer variant is forged and any acceptance fails the run
- [ ] A test that plants an acceptance (e.g. removes a validation in a fixture state) fails the probe, proving it can fire

## Size and risks
Medium; pure test-side machinery in the testkit + fuzz harness, no shipped-code path changes.
